judgements.reason: Tables 1–2 and §4.2 show only 12 seating draws per share and a favorable 1-of-1 realization, warranting draw-level uncertainty, although auditor decisions cannot automatically be resampled from reviewer votes.
The one-case world in §3.2 and Appendix B.1 cannot exercise cross-case isolation, while the abstract omits the bounds that distinguish this check from the live configuration.
Section 4.3 acknowledges the longer, conflicting colluder prompt, and §3.4 supplies non-target cases that could provide an informative control without fully isolating a causal effect of deception.
Section 3.4 does not establish auditors' exposure to reviewer-generated information or audit timing, so Table 1's seven-call standalone deployment interpretation needs clarification.
Appendix B.4 requires positive shared-minority evidence that can disappear when colluders win target votes, and §4.3 reports a false-positive cluster without an explicit run-level denominator.
Section 2's substantive comparisons depend on references that the manuscript itself flags for verification, although that flag does not establish that any identifier is a placeholder or fabricated.

Table 1 mislabels the hybrid's committee-only expectation, §6 claims judgment equivalence despite 16/17 versus zero captures, and the abstract omits Finding 1's architectural explanation of forged-receipt approval.
Section 6's judgment-equivalence statement conflicts with Table 1's 16/120 and 17/120 committee captures versus zero for gated majority on a task with no observed honest unsafe attestations.
Section 3.2 and Appendix B.1 explicitly restrict verification to one case, three seats and depth six, excluding cross-case interactions and the live seven-seat configurations.
Finding 1 explains that voters cannot verify the symmetric HMAC and identifies gated majority as the informative control, whereas the abstract reports forged approvals without that qualification.
Section 4.3 explicitly identifies hidden reasoning and the longer conflicting colluder prompt, so the abstract's monitoring suggestion needs the same non-causal qualification.

The revised concern correctly acknowledges Figure 1's existing independent-draw disclosure, while Tables 1–2 still need uncertainty treatment that separates seating variation from behavioral variation.
Section 2 acknowledges inaccessible candidate papers while asserting a combination-of-methods gap whose supporting references remain flagged for verification.

Table 1 assigns hybrid the committee-only G3 value of 21.8 even though §§3.1 and 3.4 require an additional majority gate, which cannot pass under zero honest error and a strict majority at the tested colluder shares.

Sections 1 and 6 extend assurance beyond the checked world, while §5 conflates G3's error-independence premise with G1/G2 and §3.1 establishes atomic database commits rather than external-action semantics.
Section 3.4 leaves the auditors' information set unspecified, and Table 1's request counts alone do not establish the proportional cost savings claimed in §5.
Table 1 acknowledges paired conditions and 60 independent seating draws, but neither Table 2 nor Figure 1 quantifies uncertainty in capture rates or paired regime differences.

Section 3.3 defines G2/G3 and Finding 2 explicitly reconciles 24 versus 36 pooled opportunities with 12 versus 18 capturable independent draws, so the remaining request is clarification rather than an unresolved denominator error.
Sections 3.3 and 4.3 explicitly leave G3's honest-error independence untested, and §6 nevertheless makes a broader judgment-equivalence statement than Table 1 supports.
The revised concern appropriately targets the abstract's omission of Finding 1's architectural caveat, rather than treating Table 1's existing gated-majority control as missing.

Section 3.2 and Appendix A acknowledge that the bounded same-team verification excludes larger configurations and multi-case interleavings, although Code and Data already identifies the released checker and tests.
Section 4.3 identifies the longer colluder instruction and inclusion of hidden reasoning, qualifications missing from the abstract's output-length monitoring suggestion.

The revised concern identifies genuine residual limitations in Appendix B.4's losing-side feature and §4.3's unquantified false-positive denominator despite the existing planted-signature qualification.
The now-withdrawn concern's alleged strong absence claim is not present because §4.3 calls the observations weak evidence specific to a crisp rule and Appendix A explicitly rejects generalization.
Section 2's novelty and prior-system characterizations require source verification because the manuscript acknowledges inaccessible papers and retains an explicit reference-verification note.
Table 1's hybrid prediction omits the majority gate required by §§3.1 and 3.4 and therefore is not an expected hybrid-release count.
Table 1 supplies nominal model-request counts, but §3.4 does not establish standalone auditor independence from reviewer information or corresponding token, dollar and latency costs.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Sections 3.4 and 4.2–4.3 evaluate essentially exact-match receipt judgments with no observed main-sweep honest unsafe attestations, yet §6 says random committees matched gated-majority judgment despite Table 1's 16/120 and 17/120 captures for 4-of-7 versus zero for gated majority; zero observed captures at 10% collusion also does not establish safety equivalence.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Replace equivalence language with the observed request-count–capture trade-off, state the majority threshold and tie rule, and keep G3's behavioral validity explicitly untested; clarify whether a deterministic receipt validator could classify the synthetic cases and either report that baseline or identify the experiment as a mechanism demonstration rather than semantic-oversight validation.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Section 3.3's G3 expression concerns committee approval under its behavioral assumptions, but Table 1 labels 21.8 as hybrid expected capture without marking it committee-only; hybrid release additionally requires majority approval and the remaining mechanical gates.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Label 21.8 as a committee-only opportunity estimate or replace it with not applicable; if predicting hybrid release, specify a joint model of reviewer votes and auditor attestations rather than assuming independence, noting that zero honest error and a strict majority imply zero hybrid target releases at every tested colluder share.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Section 3.4 does not establish whether committee auditors receive reviewer-generated board information or when audits occur, leaving Table 1's standalone seven-call interpretation uncertain; request counts also do not establish proportional token, dollar or latency savings.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Specify auditor prompts, information sets and audit timing across board conditions, and confirm whether committee-only deployment can omit reviewer calls; report token or dollar costs including retries if available, otherwise consistently claim fewer model requests rather than sevenfold lower cost.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Tables 1–2 and Figure 1 correctly disclose paired board conditions, but the seed structure across shares and uncertainty in capture rates and paired regime contrasts remain insufficiently documented; cross-row capture differences cannot be attributed wholly to either seating or behavior from the presented summaries.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a run-to-seed and shared-draw mapping, distinguish seating randomness from response variation, and report draw-level or appropriately clustered uncertainty and paired contrasts; preserve the existing independent-draw disclosure and only resample logged decisions when their coverage and exchangeability justify it.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Sections 1 and 6 extend assurance to arbitrary swarm sizes despite bounded implementation evidence, while §5 lists independent honest errors as an assumption of an undifferentiated guarantee; the demonstrated atomic SQLite release record also does not establish at-most-once external gateway effects.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add an assumption-and-scope table distinguishing G1, G2 and G3, attach the verification bound to the abstract's state count, and make scale-independent implementation assurance conditional on establishing the invariants beyond that bound; define release as a database transition unless concurrency and external effects have separate supporting evidence.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The one-case verification world in §3.2 and Appendix B.1 cannot exercise cross-case isolation, including erroneous reuse of another case's attestations, policy or release records; Appendix A acknowledges this exclusion, but G1's release-binding and per-case claims remain central to the assurance argument.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Clarify whether separate cross-case tests exist and report them; otherwise add a small two-case check with cross-case attestation and policy-reuse attempts plus a corresponding mutant, or explicitly distinguish cross-case isolation from properties supported by the bounded result.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The abstract's output-length monitoring suggestion omits §4.3's prompt and hidden-reasoning qualifications, and the target-only contrast cannot distinguish active manipulation from receiving the colluder instruction.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Qualify the abstract's association and use existing non-target cases to compare colluder-versus-honest output lengths when both are instructed to answer honestly; treat this as a partial control because target status and case content also differ, and reserve causal attribution for a matched-instruction design.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Section 2's novelty argument and substantive descriptions of prior systems depend on references flagged for checking and an acknowledged incomplete scan; the manuscript does not establish that any reference is fabricated.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Verify cited identifiers, titles, versions and substantive characterizations against original sources, and keep the combination-of-methods gap provisional wherever relevant comparisons remain inaccessible or unverified.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Appendix B.4's mandatory shared-minority evidence can lose signal when colluders win target votes, while §4.3 does not give an explicit run-level denominator for zero-collusion false positives; this is a voting-pattern limitation rather than a strict threshold on planted cell size.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Describe the failure regime in terms of realized losing-side votes, and report false-positive runs over all evaluated zero-collusion runs by model and board condition alongside the existing planted-signature limitation.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Section 4.3 says near-miss errors were too rare to affect any committee and that there were no errors to diversify away, whereas its table reports two 1-of-1 captures from honest errors; these statements appear inconsistent unless they refer only to larger committees or a different evaluation subset.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Specify which configurations and cases support each statement, clarify whether the no-capture observation applies only to larger committees, and document the mixed-model comparison sufficiently to interpret its null result.

rebuttals.response: I agree that seating noise warrants uncertainty estimates, but §3.4 distinguishes reviewer votes from auditor attestations, so fifty logged reviewer votes do not automatically supply fifty interchangeable auditor decisions; the resampling proposal needs a justified response model and adequate auditor coverage.

The non-target comparison is useful, but it does not directly isolate deception: §3.4 makes target status depend on case type, so target versus non-target differences can also reflect content and instruction interactions.

Source verification is scientifically necessary because §2 relies on substantive comparisons, but the editorial verification note alone does not show that the cited identifiers are placeholders or hallucinations.

Your revised concern corrects the original caption misreading, so I now agree with its residual uncertainty concern; I retain minor severity because the paper discloses pairing and avoids significance claims, and I would not label all observed capture differences seating artifacts because imperfect compliance also contributes.

There is also no strict committee-size improvement at 50% collusion under zero-error, full-compliance G3: symmetry gives a one-half capture probability for each odd-sized majority committee, so Table 2's ordering at that share is not itself a violation of a decreasing theoretical curve.

I agree about the mislabeled hybrid expectation, but shared membership alone does not fully specify dependence between votes and attestations because §3.4 collects them as separate decisions; any nonzero-error joint prediction needs an explicit response-dependence model.

Your correction of the original Table 2 interpretation is right: 12/13 denotes DeepSeek/gpt-oss, not visible/hidden conditions; B's revised concern no longer relies on that error, and the auditor-information clarification remains valid.

I continue to disagree with treating the denominator reconciliation as a major unresolved defect: Finding 2 explicitly gives twelve realized versus eighteen expected capturable draws, doubled to twenty-four versus thirty-six paired opportunities; a compact summation formula would improve reproducibility, but compliance adjustment is not required for the explicitly full-compliance G3 prediction.

I agree that G3 remains unvalidated, but honest-error independence is not required by mechanical G1 or the conditional zero-error G2 implication, so correlated-error concerns should remain attached to the appropriate claim.

I agree with the revised minor abstract-scoping concern; Table 1 already contains the informative crowd-plus-mechanical-check control, while a public-key or tool-assisted voter experiment would extend applicability rather than repair a missing control in the existing comparison.

The losing-side limitation is real, but Appendix B.4 does not impose a hard less-than-50% planted-cell assumption: imperfect compliance and case-specific outcomes determine whether shared-minority evidence remains available.
